subject: WellSpan trial: fit assessment, hosting decision path and operational owners
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@wellspanhealth.org>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Recap & proposal — WellSpan trial: success criteria and hosting options

Alex — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and a proposed next steps plan so everyone is aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Key takeaways:
- Primary goal: validate Redwood inference for patient-summary extraction and clinical search in an initial POC (2–4 weeks).
- Data: sample de-identified notes + a locked set of 250 live records for accuracy checks.
- Success metrics (proposed): precision@5 for retrieval >= 0.85, extraction F1 >= 0.80, 95th pct latency (friendly UI flow) < 400ms for typical requests.
- Security constraints: WellSpan needs SOC 2 evidence, audit logs retention for 12 months, and KMS integration for keys.
- Expected throughput: pilot ~50–200 QPS peak; sustained ~20 QPS.

Hosting options discussed (short guidance):
1) Hosted API (fastest onboarding) — 48–72 hour setup, limited network isolation, logs in our control plane with export. Good for quick validation.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity) — predictable throughput, can isolate workload, supports stricter logging retention windows. Requires a week to provision.
3) VPC/private deployment — best for strict data residency/PII needs and complete control of keys/audit logs. On-prem or VPC options; longer timeline (~3–6 weeks depending on approvals).

Our recommendation for this POC: start with Hosted API to validate function and quality (week 1), then transition to a Dedicated sandbox for throughput and audit log commitments if tests look good (week 2–3). If WellSpan procurement requires a VPC from day one due to policy, we can parallel-path the VPC assessment but that will add time.

Proposed POC plan and owners (short):
- Week 0 (this week): share success criteria spreadsheet (attached), confirm sample data transfer method and NDA scope — owner: Alex (WellSpan) + Laura (SE).
- Week 1: quality validation on hosted API, iterate prompts and eval sets — owner: Laura (SE).
- Week 2: performance/load tests; decide if we need Dedicated sandbox — owner: Ben (Sales Ops) + Infra Eng.
- Week 3: security checklist and evidence handoff (SOC2 artifacts, logs, key provisioning) — owner: Security & Alex/Procurement.

Next steps (please confirm by EOD):
- Alex to confirm whether procurement requires VPC on day 1 or allows hosted first.
- WellSpan to confirm who will own data transfer and whether STMP/OAuth will be used for file upload.
- Redwood to provision temporary hosted credentials and a shared evaluation Doc (link below).

Attachments: wellspan-poc-success-criteria.xlsx (local metrics and eval cases) and MAP stub (mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf).

Links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB_example_shared_doc

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@wellspanhealth.org>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: J. Morales <j.morales@wellspanhealth.org>, Procurement Team <procurement@wellspanhealth.org>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap & proposal — WellSpan trial: success criteria and hosting options

Thanks Markus — useful summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement: we typically require VPC or customer-managed network for any environment that touches live PHI. For a short pilot using only de-identified records we can accept a hosted test environment, but Procurement wants a clear path to VPC/dedicated infra before we go live in production. They also asked for expected SLAs and an incident escalation path.
- Security: SOC 2 report + current penetration test summary would be needed for our security review. Also, can Redwood support a KMS integration (we have Azure Key Vault and AWS KMS depending on environment)?
- Timeline: our product team is aiming to start active testing the week of Sep 27. Is that feasible?

I will confirm who on our side will be the data owner (probably J. Morales) and loop in procurement formally if we move forward.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Sr. Product Manager, Clinical Search | WellSpan Health
alex.chen@wellspanhealth.org
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@wellspanhealth.org>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap & proposal — WellSpan trial: success criteria and hosting options

Alex — appreciate the clarifications. Quick responses and a concrete ops proposal below.

Security and compliance:
- SOC 2: we will share the most recent SOC 2 Type II report via a secure link (I will route to procurement).
- Pen tests: we can provide the executive summary of our recent third-party penetration test. Full report requires an NDA/PO.
- KMS: Redwood supports both AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault for private deployments; Hosted API supports envelope encryption and customer-managed keys via an HSM integration for Dedicated/VPC.

On timeline and hosting:
- Week of Sep 27 start is feasible if WellSpan accepts a hosted pilot for week 1 and data transfer is completed by Sep 24. To meet that date we need: signed SOW or trial acceptance, sample dataset, and confirmation of success criteria.
- If Procurement insists on VPC from day 1, we should target a Sep 27 exploratory kickoff (arch review) but expect provisioning and network approvals to push functional testing into mid-Oct.

Recommended operational playbook (concise):
1) Day 0–2: NDA/SOW sign, Redwood creates hosted trial credentials, and we confirm data upload method (SFTP or secure Share). Link to shared eval doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB_example_shared_doc
2) Day 3–9: Prompt tuning and quality eval on hosted API; weekly checkpoints with WellSpan (Laura).
3) Day 10–16: Performance testing and decision gate — if perf > threshold or procurement demands isolation, spin up Dedicated sandbox (Ben coordinates).
4) Security handoff: provide SOC2 artifacts, pen test summary, and configuration checklist for KMS/audit logs.

Owners: Laura (SE) — technical lead for evals and data QA; Ben (Sales Ops) — provisioning dedicated resources / commercial discussions; Markus (AE) — contract / timeline owner; WellSpan: Alex (PM) + J. Morales (data owner) + Procurement (legal/IT).

Attachments: I added an internal infra note and a short runbook for hosted -> dedicated transition. See mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf for milestones.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
